findings.title: In a field made with `Field::binary`, products and inverses branch on the bits of an operand, so the time to check or correct a word depends on its symbols
findings.affected: src/field/binary.rs:51-63 (`multiply`) and 67-77 (`inverse`), reached through `Field::multiply` and `Field::inverse` (src/field.rs:137-163); callers with symbols or values derived from them as the first operand: src/cyclic/decode.rs:128, 131, 223, 240, 326, 333; src/cyclic/owned.rs:338, 341; src/correct.rs:420, 438. Only `Field::Binary`, that is `Field::binary` with anything other than (8, 0x11D) or (11, 0x805); x86-64, rustc 1.99.1, release and LTO builds.
findings.reproduction: Harness `timing` (docs/audits/AUD-006-harnesses/timing): `cargo build --release --bin timing`, then `taskset -c 3 target/release/timing`. It times `CyclicWords::correct_word` on 2,048 clean all-zero words and on 2,048 random valid words, 41 interleaved rounds. Assembly: `cargo rustc --release --lib -- --emit asm -C codegen-units=1` shows `and %r9d,%r14d; je` (r9d = 1 << degree, r10d = the polynomial) in the Binary arm of `Field::multiply`, and the same four times in `Field::inverse`; an LTO program built as RUST-12 asks (panic = abort, codegen-units = 1) shows the same jumps.
findings.expected: src/field/binary.rs:1-3: products and inverses use "masks and fixed chains, never tables or branches on an element"; src/correct.rs:3-4: "The arithmetic never branches on shard bytes"; docs/TECHNICAL.md limits decoder timing to error-dependent results. The register marks AUD-002-SEC006 verified because "the claim covers … single products and inverses".
findings.observed: For GF(2^10) made by `Field::binary`, checking a word that has no errors takes 2.84 to 2.86 times as long for random words as for all-zero words (two runs of the reviewer, one of the coordinator). For the named GF(2^11) the ratio is 1.00 (0.98 to 1.03). The named fields' arms use shifts, SIMD and conditional moves.
findings.impact: A process that shares the CPU can learn about the symbols of data a program handles in a field of its own choice, through timing and branch-predictor state; the strict mode accepts such fields. QR codes (GF(2^8)) and MHFE-REPAIR-1 (GF(2^11)) are not affected. No symbol was recovered; only the dependence was shown. The named fields are branch-free because of today's code generation, and no check holds them so. A regression of AUD-002-SEC006.
findings.evidence: Harness `timing`; reviewer's assembly listings (machine-local); coordinator's rerun: GF(2048) 2,043/2,042 ns, ratio 1.00; GF(2^10) 2,110/6,012 ns, ratio 2.86.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the reduction mask opaque to the optimiser in src/field/binary.rs (`core::hint::black_box`, or reduce at a fixed bit position after shifting the element left by 16 − m), and add a check that keeps every arm free of jumps on operand bits. Until then, state the limit in docs/TECHNICAL.md and SECURITY.md, and correct the comments at binary.rs:1-3 and correct.rs:3-4.
findings.requiredVerification: The timing harness gives a ratio near 1.00 for GF(2^10); the release and LTO assembly of `Field::multiply` and `Field::inverse` shows no jump on an operand bit in any arm.

findings.title: Publishing this tree would put a second, unsigned 0.1.0 under the version that the signed GitHub release and the deleted crates.io upload already hold
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The package that would be uploaded is not the signed and attested one, and the version is taken.
findings.affected: Cargo.toml:3 (`version = "0.1.0"`); CHANGELOG.md:3-7 (an Unreleased entry above 0.1.0); docs/API.md:33 and README.md:60 (instructions and figures for 0.1.0).
findings.reproduction: `cargo package --offline --locked --allow-dirty --no-verify` gives reed-solomon-core-0.1.0.crate with SHA-256 b2296a6d54b031ac93954617fecd9fa4bde3d853ca98ca16798dbd5790bbed32. The GitHub release v0.1.0 asset has SHA-256 6eadca15712b550f8a4bc7cf6cd232023dd4726d61095dfaa23caf22bae19be8, attested by release.yml run 43804427212 at a55d636. The deleted crates.io upload was 552e69cc…, and the local crates.io index cache still lists 0.1.0 (published 2026-11-16T03:48:14Z). The publish dry run (publish-dry-run.log) packaged 0.1.0 and reached "Uploading" without a warning.
findings.expected: One version, one archive: a crates.io package equals the signed and attested archive of its version, or carries a new version with its own tag, signature and attestation (CHECK-BLD-005).
findings.observed: 8 of the 87 packaged files differ from the signed archive: the normalised Cargo.toml and Cargo.toml.orig (the dependency requirements), .cargo_vcs_info.json, CHANGELOG.md, README.md, SECURITY.md, docs/API.md and docs/README.md. The documented `gpg --verify reed-solomon-core-0.1.0.crate.asc` step would fail on it, and neither SHA256SUMS nor the attestation covers it.
findings.impact: Three byte-different archives would carry the name reed-solomon-core 0.1.0; crates.io does not let a version be replaced or used again, so the upload would be refused, or, were it taken, a lock file pinned to the deleted upload would fail its checksum. The code (src/, tests/, examples/, Cargo.lock) is the same in all three.
findings.evidence: Release reviewer's package comparison and digests (machine-local); publish-dry-run.log; the GitHub release and attestation API, read only.
findings.recommendedFix: Release this tree as 0.1.1: a dated CHANGELOG heading, the 0.1.0 references at docs/API.md:33 and README.md:60 updated, a commit, a signed tag v0.1.1, the attestation of release.yml, and `cargo publish` from a clean checkout of that tag.
findings.requiredVerification: `cargo package` of the tag gives the attested digest; after the upload the crates.io index `cksum` equals it; the documented `gh attestation verify` command passes.

findings.title: The release workflow attests a tag without running the CI gates
findings.reproduction: Static review: release.yml runs on tags `v*` and only runs `cargo package --locked`; it has no `needs:` on CI, no `workflow_call` and no check of CI's result; ci.yml runs on branches, pull requests and by hand, never on tags; the repository has no rulesets.
findings.expected: CHECK-BLD-005: the normal release path cannot bypass the mandatory gates.
findings.observed: A tag on a commit whose CI failed, or never ran, still gets an attested package. v0.1.0 was attested twice (run 43802177681 at 664ebb1, run 43804427212 at a55d636). No bypass happened: CI passed at a55d636 (run 43804427792).
findings.impact: A broken commit could be released with a valid attestation; the attestation then says where a package was built, not that it passed the tests.
findings.evidence: release.yml and ci.yml, read; the GitHub API, read only.
findings.recommendedFix: Make ci.yml callable (`workflow_call`) and let the packaging job depend on it, or check CI's conclusion for `$GITHUB_SHA` before packaging.

findings.title: The compatible requirements are explained by a one-copy promise they do not decide, and drop CORE-25's exact pins for what secret safety rests on without a recorded reason
findings.affected: Cargo.toml:26-38 and CHANGELOG.md:5-7 (working tree); docs/audits/README.md rows AUD-001-BLD002 and AUD-002-SEC005.
findings.reproduction: Probes of the security reviewer (harness `one-copy` and machine-local variants): a library requiring `secret-protection-core = "=0.1.0"` and a program requiring `"0.1"` also build one copy (one lock entry, equal `Secret` TypeIds); a library pinning `libc = "=0.2.190"` with a program needing 0.2.191 fails to resolve; the protection crate taken by the program from a path and by this crate from the registry gives two copies under caret requirements too (two lock entries, two `before_main` entries in `.init_array`, `E0277: Secret: Held is not satisfied`); with secret-protection-core 0.1.0, a program requiring zeroize 1.9.2 fails to resolve.
findings.expected: CORE-25: a library on crates.io takes caret requirements, and "only what the protocol or the safety of secrets rests on stays exact"; the changelog says what a change does.
findings.observed: sha2, zeroize and secret-protection-core became caret requirements. The changelog's reason, one copy of the protection crate, holds with exact pins too, and fails with a path or git source either way. What the change does give is that a program can resolve a later 0.1.x and the fixes of the dependencies. Cargo.lock still holds secret-protection-core 0.1.0 and zeroize 1.9.1, while 0.1.1 is out.
findings.impact: No secret is affected today. From the next 0.1.x on, a program may run the strict mode with a protection crate that this crate's strict tests did not run with; the changelog misleads a program built from sibling checkouts.
findings.recommendedFix: Reword the changelog and the Cargo.toml comment to say what the requirements do; record the reason for leaving CORE-25's exception; require secret-protection-core "0.1.1", update Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock, and run the strict tests with them before publishing.
findings.requiredVerification: Review of the text; the strict tests pass with the new lock files.

findings.title: The documents no longer say that a vote takes two new protected buffers at every change of holders, which a crafted pile turns into about 100 times the time per counted step
findings.affected: src/file/set/vote.rs:346-356 (a new `Finder` whenever the holders change, charged `rates.weights()` only) and src/correct.rs:232, 235 (its two `Buffer`s); docs/TECHNICAL.md ("Work limits for file sets"), docs/API.md:456 and SECURITY.md:25.
findings.reproduction: Harness `files`, program `holders`: `cargo build --release --bin holders`, then `target/release/holders 100000` (and 400000). GF(2^8), k = 1, 1-byte blocks, files of shards 0, 1 and 2, one bit flipped in block b of shard 1 for odd b and of shard 2 for even b, so that the holders alternate between {0, 2} and {0, 1}.
findings.expected: The remediation of AUD-001-ARC002 kept the design and named its cost: "A vote makes a new search, with syndromes and a room of its own, each time the shards that hold a block change" (79dd2f5:docs/TECHNICAL.md:272). With the same paragraph went the AUD-001-API001 note that tens of thousands of `Buffer`s in one call reach the system's mapping limit and the call answers `Memory`.
findings.observed: Both notes were removed in 664ebb1, before the v0.1.0 tag. With `protect`, 100,000 alternating blocks take 1.55 to 4.45 s for 13,400,000 counted steps (115 to 332 ns per step), against 0.9 to 2.3 ns per step when the holders stay the same; alloc only: 3.1 against 1.1 ns. `vote.steps()` stays within `vote_work`.
findings.impact: Availability only, linear in the blocks, no wrong answer. A program that sizes its limit from `vote_work`, as SECURITY.md:25 advises for files from outside, gets about two orders of magnitude more time than the counted steps suggest.
findings.recommendedFix: Restore both notes in docs/TECHNICAL.md, with a clause in the `vote_work` row of docs/API.md and at SECURITY.md:25; or keep the decoder's two buffers across changes of holders, or charge a stated step cost per new search in `vote_work` and `vote`.
findings.requiredVerification: The notes are present; for a code change, the alternating pile runs within a small factor of the stable one and `vote_known_answer` still gives 945.

findings.title: `FileError::Field` says that a field of `Field::binary` has no shard file, though `Field::binary(8, None)` is `Gf256` and has one
findings.affected: src/file.rs:33-35; src/file/facts.rs:62-63 and docs/API.md:307 (`SetFacts::new` names only GF(2^11) as refused).
findings.reproduction: Harness `files`: `target/debug/aud006-files-probe fields`: `binary(8, None)` and `binary(8, Some(0x11D))` are `Gf256` and `SetFacts::new` accepts them; `binary(8, Some(0x12B))`, `binary(4, None)`, `binary(16, None)` and `binary(11, None)` give `Err(Field)`.
findings.expected: docs/API.md:884 states the behaviour correctly; the rustdoc agrees with it.
findings.observed: The rustdoc says the opposite for GF(2^8) by 0x11D, and `new` omits the refusal of every `Field::Binary` field.
findings.impact: Documentation only: a program may avoid a valid field or expect `Field` for it.
findings.recommendedFix: Say "the `Field::Binary` variant has none", and for `new` "fails for a field other than Gf256 and Gf65536" in both places.
findings.requiredVerification: Review of the rustdoc and API text.

findings.title: The rustdoc of `Mark` says a marked symbol may hold any bytes, but both plans refuse a marked symbol outside the field
findings.affected: src/correct/plan.rs:16; behaviour at src/correct/plan.rs:92 and src/cyclic/owned.rs:267.
findings.reproduction: Harness `codes`, program `mark_doc`: `Code::plan` and `CyclicCode::plan` with a marked symbol 0xFFFF give `Err(Symbol)`; with 0x0000, or with the shard named lost, they plan; `CyclicWords::correct_word` accepts 0xFFFF as an erasure. tests/suite/plans.rs:462-471 asserts the refusal.
findings.expected: docs/API.md:88, 163 and 871: marked values must still fit the field.
findings.observed: docs.rs promises the opposite of what the calls do.
findings.impact: A program written from docs.rs that marks an unreadable GF(2^11) word with a sentinel gets `Err(Symbol)` instead of a plan; nothing is changed and no wrong data results.
findings.recommendedFix: Say that a marked symbol must still hold an element of the field, such as zero, and that its value does not change the plan.
findings.requiredVerification: Review of `cargo doc`; the existing assertion keeps the behaviour.

findings.title: The root re-export `Zeroize` serves no type of the crate
findings.reproduction: `grep -rn 'impl Zeroize' src` finds none; nightly rustdoc JSON shows no type implementing it and no signature or bound naming it; tests, examples and fuzz targets do not use it. `impl Zeroize for Change` was removed in 57409cd (the AUD-002-SEC003 fix); the re-export dates from 4969ec8.
findings.expected: A public export serves the API (CHECK-ARC-002).
findings.observed: The export has no use in the crate's API.
findings.impact: It keeps zeroize's major version in the public API, and removing it later is a breaking change.
findings.recommendedFix: Document its purpose with an example (wiping buffers a caller lends), or drop it at the next breaking version.

informationalObservations: MHFE-REPAIR-1: all 16 cards (sizes 2, 4, 6 and 8 of four containers) and all 3 repairs of mhfe_spec's vectors/profiles/repair-words.json (SHA-256 fa4f77a5…, as its SHA256SUMS says) come out of `CyclicCode` and `CyclicWords` as published, by five paths each for the repairs. Against mhfe_core's own decoder (src/repair/field.rs, copied into the harness), 24,000 random containers of 12 to 24 words, every card size and damage up to 2e + s = k + 2 gave the same parity and the same decoding in every case (17,634 words found, 1,501 of them beyond the bound by both; 6,366 found by neither).

One copy of secret-protection-core: a program that takes this crate (path, default features) and `secret-protection-core = "0.1"` from crates.io builds one copy: one lock entry, one `before_main` in `.init_array`, the program's `Secret` accepted as `Held`. The crate never calls `Isolation::enter*`, `Worker`, `serve` or `write_secret`; after a program isolates itself, a strict encode still works. Two copies arise only from a path or git source, or from an incompatible 0.2, and then fail safe at compile time.
secret-protection-core 0.1.1 (crates.io, 2026-11-24) changes only its manifest (no change under src/ since 0.1.0) and takes caret requirements for its own dependencies.
The two RustSec warnings (instant 0.1.13, lru 0.7.8) come only through the test oracle reed-solomon-erasure 6.0.0; no normal dependency has them.

The suite's independent oracle, reed-solomon-erasure 6.0.0, covers GF(2^8) and GF(2^16) only; GF(2^11) and the other binary fields rest on literal answers and self-consistency, which the codes harness covered.
`Code::correct` has no work limit; near 65,536 shards a call may take long (not measured).
A pile of 200,000 header-only files took about 1,656 bytes of memory per file, mostly unused capacity; a program that accepts many small files from others should cap their number.
`Correction::Corrected` of the cyclic code counts lost places whose value was already right; docs/API.md says so, the rustdoc does not.
Coverage reproduced: 98.23 % (5,984 of 6,092 lines), as docs/COVERAGE.md states for the release tree.
limitations: Linux x86-64 only: macOS, Windows, Android, iOS and WebAssembly were not run natively; CI on GitHub runs the tests on Linux AArch64, macOS and Windows.
Constant-time behaviour was checked on x86-64 with rustc 1.99.1; AArch64 was not checked.
The OpenPGP signatures and SHA256SUMS of the GitHub release were not downloaded or verified; the attestation was read through the API.
Forced allocation failure part-way through a call, Miri, and statistical timing tests beyond the interleaved probe were not run.
secret-protection-core was reviewed only where this crate uses it.
Three reviewers were interrupted by a restart of the coordinating session and resumed from their saved context; the snapshot was checked unchanged before and after.
This is an AI-assisted review, not an independent human security audit.
